title: Precis of Investigation, American Consulate-General, Shanghai, 20 July 1935
creator: U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service and correspondents
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives at San Francisco, Records of the Immigration and Naturalization Service (RG 85), Immigration Arrival Investigation Case File 35527/15-16, National Archives Identifier 28882547 (page 135 of 139)
alt_text: 1935 Shanghai consulate visa form with a photo of eighteen-year-old Ieoh-ming Pe, signed by him.
long_description: Typed form headed 'American Consulate-General, Shanghai, China. July 20, 1935. Precis of Investigation.' Name: Pe, Ieoh-ming, with his name in Chinese characters. Nationality Chinese; Class Student; birthplace Canton. Education: graduated St. John's Middle School 1934, attended St. John's University. Plans: University of Pennsylvania, six years. Financial support: 'Full support is to be provided by applicant's father, Tsuyee Pei, manager of the Bank of China, who is very well fixed finanacially' [sic]. Photograph of a smiling young man in a jacket and tie, signed 'Ieohming Pe'. Intended departure: President Coolidge, 13 August 1935, to San Francisco. Signed by Vice Consul James B. Pilcher.
gloss: The anchor: the first page of his American story, with his teenage photograph and signature.

title: Radiogram, University of Pennsylvania to St. John's University, Shanghai: 'Ieohmingpe admission approved', July 1935
creator: U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service and correspondents
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives at San Francisco, Records of the Immigration and Naturalization Service (RG 85), Immigration Arrival Investigation Case File 35527/15-16, National Archives Identifier 28882547 (page 137 of 139)
alt_text: Torn 1935 radiogram reading 'IEOHMINGPE ADMISSION APPROVED UNIVERSITY PENNA'.
long_description: Printed radiogram form, 'World Wide Wireless, Chinese Government Radio Administration, Sassoon House, Shanghai', stamped 1935 Jul 9, sent from Philadelphia to St. John's University Shanghai. The lower right corner is torn away.
gloss: The telegram that let him apply for a visa — and the misspelling 'Pe' that followed him for years.

title: Arrival statement, Immigration and Naturalization Service, San Francisco, 28 August 1935 (Form SF2602)
creator: U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service and correspondents
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives at San Francisco, Records of the Immigration and Naturalization Service (RG 85), Immigration Arrival Investigation Case File 35527/15-16, National Archives Identifier 28882547 (page 136 of 139)
alt_text: Handwritten 1935 San Francisco arrival questionnaire, signed by Pei in Chinese and English.
long_description: Form SF2602, case 35527/15-16, ex S.S. President Coolidge, 28 August 1935, class 'Student 4(e)'. Answers in an inspector's hand: names 'Pe Ieoh Ming - no others'; 'Never married'; children 'None'. A printed note warns that his answers could be used if he later testified about family relationships with a Chinese resident — 'So advised'. Signed by the applicant in Chinese characters and as 'Pe Ieoh Ming'; inspector H. Schmidt; interpreter 'None used'.
gloss: Questions written for the Chinese Exclusion era, asked of an eighteen-year-old student.

title: 'In re: Ieoh Ming Pei — Change of Status', Immigration and Naturalization Service, 2 October 1946 (page 1)
creator: U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service and correspondents
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives at San Francisco, Records of the Immigration and Naturalization Service (RG 85), Immigration Arrival Investigation Case File 35527/15-16, National Archives Identifier 28882547 (page 12 of 139)
alt_text: Typed 1946 immigration memo on Pei's student status and Harvard's request that he stay.
long_description: Memo headed 'San Francisco – 35527/15-16, October 2, 1946. In re: Ieoh Ming Pei. Change of Status.' Describes 'the above named 29 year old married male, native and citizen of China, Chinese race' admitted at San Francisco on 28 August 1935 for two years as a student, with extensions to 28 August 1946. Harvard asks that he remain as a teaching fellow at $4000 a year. 'It is understood that the subject expects to return to China to teach after this year's work at Harvard.'
gloss: Eleven years after arriving, the government still expected him to go home.

title: Letter from Joseph Hudnut, Dean of the Faculty of Design, Harvard University, to the Immigration and Naturalization Office, Boston, 8 May 1947
creator: U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service and correspondents
rights_statement_verbatim: Access Restriction(s): Unrestricted. Use Restriction(s): Unrestricted.
required_credit: National Archives at San Francisco, Records of the Immigration and Naturalization Service (RG 85), Immigration Arrival Investigation Case File 35527/15-16, National Archives Identifier 28882547 (page 8 of 139)
alt_text: Typed 1947 letter from Harvard's Dean of Design asking that Pei be allowed to stay.
long_description: Harvard University letterhead, Graduate School of Design, Office of the Dean, May 8 1947. 'I am writing to you in behalf of Mr. Ieoh Ming Pei, who is applying for resident status in the United States... we hope that he may be permitted to stay in this country in order to continue his teaching of architecture in this School, as Assistant Professor of Architecture.' Signed Joseph Hudnut.
gloss: Harvard asks the government to let him stay.
